name: question words
title: Spanish Question Words Practice: Qué, Cuál, Dónde, Cuándo Quiz
description: Practice Spanish question words: qué, cuál, quién, dónde, adónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo and por qué, with accents, a rule table and 10 sentences checked as you tap.
answer: Spanish question words always carry a written accent: qué, quién, cuál, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué. Quién and cuál have plurals (quiénes, cuáles), and cuánto agrees with the noun (cuántas personas). Use qué for definitions and before nouns, cuál for choosing from a set, and adónde with movement.

rulesCaption: Question words and what they ask

quiz.why: Asking for one item of information (a name, a number, an address) with ser: cuál.

quiz.after: no viniste a la fiesta? —Porque estaba enfermo.
quiz.why: Why in a question: por qué, two words with accent.

quiz.after: es una quinceañera? —Una fiesta de quince años.
quiz.why: Asking for a definition: qué es.

mistakes: Leaving out the accent: «¿Donde vives?» should be «¿Dónde vives?»; question words always carry it, even inside a sentence (no sé dónde está).
Using qué with ser for information: «¿Qué es tu nombre?» should be «¿Cuál es tu nombre?»
Writing porque in a question: «¿Porque lloras?» should be «¿Por qué lloras?»; porque (one word) answers.
Forgetting agreement: «¿Cuántos personas?» should be «¿Cuántas personas?»
Skipping the opening question mark: Spanish questions start with ¿.

heritage: Heritage speakers usually ask questions perfectly in speech; the writing points are the accents (qué, cómo, cuándo also in indirect questions: no sé cuándo llega) and the four forms of por qué, porque, porqué and por que.
teacher: Pairs interview each other with one card per question word and must use all of them. Then each student introduces their partner to the class from the answers.

faq.question: What is the difference between qué and cuál?
faq.answer: Before a noun, use qué: ¿qué libro? Before ser, qué asks for a definition (¿qué es un mole?) and cuál asks for a specific item, like a name, a number or a date: ¿cuál es tu teléfono?

faq.question: Do question words always have an accent?
faq.answer: Yes, when they ask, directly or indirectly: ¿Dónde vives? No sé dónde vive. Without the accent they are relative words: la casa donde vivo, cuando llego.

faq.question: What is the difference between dónde and adónde?
faq.answer: Dónde asks where something is (¿dónde estás?); adónde asks where to, with movement verbs like ir (¿adónde vas?). In speech, many people use dónde for both, which is widely accepted.
